title: Can This Code See That Member?
blurb: The real test: given where the calling code lives — same class, a derived class, an unrelated class, same or different assembly — does the access compile, or is it a CS0122 error? Read each pair and predict.

levels.title: L1 · private, from another class
levels.prompt: Both classes are in the same assembly. Does this compile?

blocks.label: The caller — a different, unrelated class

failStates.title: private means only inside Account
failStates.explain: private limits access to the containing type itself. Report is a separate class, so `a._balance` is a CS0122 'inaccessible due to its protection level' error — even in the same assembly.

levels.title: L2 · protected, across assemblies
levels.prompt: Square is in a DIFFERENT assembly than Shape, and derives from it. Does this compile?

blocks.label: Assembly 1
Assembly 2 (references Assembly 1)

failStates.title: protected crosses assembly boundaries
failStates.explain: protected grants access to derived classes in ANY assembly. Square derives from Shape and uses Sides through its own inheritance, so it compiles. The assembly boundary only matters for internal.

levels.title: L3 · internal, across assemblies
levels.prompt: Loader is in a different assembly and does NOT derive from Config. Does this compile?

blocks.label: Assembly 1
Assembly 2 (references Assembly 1)

failStates.title: internal stops at the assembly boundary
failStates.explain: internal means 'anyone in the SAME assembly.' Assembly 2 is a different assembly, so Key is inaccessible (CS0122). Assembly 1 could opt in explicitly with [InternalsVisibleTo("Assembly2")].

levels.title: L4 · protected internal — the OR
levels.prompt: Tools is in the SAME assembly but does NOT derive from BaseApi. Does this compile?

blocks.label: The member
Same assembly, NOT a derived class

failStates.title: protected internal is OR, not AND
failStates.explain: protected internal = protected OR internal. Tools isn't derived, but it IS in the same assembly, so the 'internal' half alone grants access. Either condition is enough.

levels.title: L5 · private protected — the AND
levels.prompt: Plugin derives from BaseApi, but lives in a DIFFERENT assembly. Does this compile?

blocks.label: Assembly 1
Assembly 2 (references Assembly 1)

failStates.title: private protected needs BOTH conditions
failStates.explain: private protected = protected AND internal: you must be a derived class AND in the same assembly. Plugin derives, but it's in another assembly, so it fails the 'same assembly' half — CS0122.
